title: Transactions, staged mutation and recovery
summary: The native transaction line preserves NOTEXECUTED versus ROLLEDBACK, staged/atomic mutation publication, recovery journals and ordered mutation evidence. Placement of transaction semantics at the shared database boundary must not erase NoSQLServer's richer native diagnostic/result surface. In the selected writable SQLite v0.91 candidate, one SQL mutation batch holds SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE, compares the selected table's schema plus every row against the immutable selection snapshot, and atomically commits NoSQL-approved prepared DML only on equality; changed rows and phantom rows cause rollback.
invariants: A request rejected before operation begins is NOTEXECUTED.
A transaction that began and was atomically undone is ROLLEDBACK.
Those states must never be collapsed.
Interop is additive; native planner/recovery evidence remains available.
Table-wide equality validation guards single-table predicate mutation against concurrent inserts, including zero-match selections; it is conservative and may reject unrelated same-table changes.
A conflict must roll back the entire batch. A committed mutation whose later snapshot refresh fails remains COMMITTED, never a falsely retryable failure.
Do not call this global serializability: multi-table predicates, multi-statement transactions, external-dependent predicates and distributed mesh access remain outside the qualified contract.

provenance.claim: BEGIN IMMEDIATE predicate guard and failure semantics.
